name: MongoDB Atlas
summary: MongoDB Atlas is a fully hosted version of MongoDB, a database that stores data as flexible, JSON-like documents.

free_plan_covers.note: Free M0 cluster: 512 MB storage, 100 operations per second, and 10 GB data transfer in and out every 7 days.

first_paid_usd_month.note: The cheapest paid tier, Flex, is billed hourly by usage with no flat monthly fee; continuous use runs about $8 to $30/month.

portability.note: MongoDB's document format is widely supported elsewhere, and the free MongoDB Community Edition can be self-hosted.

storage_model.note: MongoDB runs and manages the database servers for you in the cloud.

data_model.note: MongoDB stores data as JSON-like documents rather than rows in tables.

realtime_built_in.note: Change Streams let your server watch for changes, but you must build and host your own relay to push updates into a browser.

serverless_friendly.note: The official Node driver supports connection caching for serverless functions; a standalone HTTP Data API was retired in 2025.

mobile_sdk.note: The Atlas Device SDK (formerly Realm) for mobile apps was deprecated and reached end of life on September 30, 2025.

setup.step: Create a free MongoDB Atlas account and an M0 cluster.
Get the cluster's connection string from Atlas under Database, then Connect, then Drivers.
Install the official MongoDB driver package in your Next.js app.
Add the connection string to your environment file.
Open one MongoClient connection at module scope and reuse it across requests instead of reconnecting each time.

builder_notes: Never expose MONGODB_URI or use the driver directly in browser code; keep database access in server components, API routes, or route handlers.
Cache the MongoClient at module scope so serverless functions reuse one pooled connection instead of exhausting the connection limit.
Free clusters auto-pause after 30 days of no activity; data is kept but you must manually resume the cluster to use it again.
